Agents.incomplete_history: History is incomplete or unavailable. Counts cover only stored observations in the selected period.
Agents.partial_run: Some observations may be missing. This trace does not establish a complete conversation outcome.
Agents.usage_scope: Latest observed provider response; not a call total
Agents.event_limit: The view limit has been reached. Refresh to return to the first events.
Agents.generated_audio: Assistant text represents generated speech. Interrupted speech may not have been heard in full. Caller text is automated transcription.
Agents.delete_confirm: Delete this transcript permanently? Run metadata remains until its retention expires. Capture will not resume for this run.
Agents.handoff_scope: A committed handoff ends agent ownership. Its outcome does not describe the subsequent human conversation.
Agents.saved_pending: Settings saved. Synchronization is pending; the service will retry automatically.
Agents.retention_help: Settings apply to existing history too. Shorter retention can permanently remove expired data. Allowed range: 1–365 days.
Agents.capture_help: Capture is off by default. OpenAI Realtime is supported; Grok remains metadata only. Enabling caller transcription can add provider charges.
Agents.capture_internal: Enable transcripts for the Internal agent
Agents.capture_external: Enable transcripts for the External agent
Agents.capture_revocation: Enabling applies to new runs. Disabling stops active capture when synchronization completes; already stored text keeps its retention. Delete it from a run to remove it sooner.

Agents.connectors_description: Define business services and the operations agents may call. Add a credential, save and publish a connector, then grant its operations to an agent.

help.enable_integrations: Enable business connector calls and new API runs. Save to apply. When disabled, new requests and connector calls are blocked; saved configuration is kept.
help.credential_id: A permanent name for this secret, for example business-key or openai-key. Use 1–48 lowercase letters, digits, hyphens or underscores, starting with a letter. Reference this ID in a connector or API agent.
help.credential_value: The API key or token supplied by the business service or OpenAI. It is encrypted when saved and is not shown again. To replace it, add a new credential ID and update the configuration using it.
help.connector_id: Permanent identifier for this business service, for example helpdesk. Use 1–48 lowercase letters, digits, hyphens or underscores, starting with a letter. It cannot be changed after the first save.
help.connector_name: A readable name shown to administrators, for example Customer support service. The connector ID identifies it in permissions and API configuration.
help.service_origin: The business API server, for example https://helpdesk.example.com. HTTPS is required; port 443 or 8443 is allowed. Put endpoint paths in each operation, not here.
help.connector_credential: Select the saved key or token for this business service. Add it in Credentials first. The secret is sent only to the configured service using the authentication method below.
help.authentication: Choose how the business service accepts its credential. Bearer sends Authorization: Bearer saved-secret. API key sends the secret in the custom header specified below.
help.header_name: Header required by the service for its API key, for example X-API-Key. Enter only the header name; its value comes from the selected credential.
help.private_networks: Optional private network ranges this service may resolve to, separated by commas, for example 10.20.0.0/16. Leave blank for public servers. Use private IPv4 ranges /16 or narrower, or private IPv6 ranges /48 or narrower; loopback and link-local addresses are blocked.
help.operation_id: Unique identifier within this connector, for example lookup or create_ticket. Use 1–48 lowercase letters, digits, hyphens or underscores, starting with a letter. Agents and grants refer to this operation and its published version.
help.operation_description: Explain what this operation does and when the agent should use it, for example Look up an authorized customer by ID. This description is shown to the language model.
help.method: GET reads data. POST creates a business record, such as a ticket, and requires write permission. Choose the method required by the business API.
help.operation_path: Endpoint path added to the service origin, for example /customers/{customer_id} or /tickets. Braces refer to fields in the input schema. Put query parameters in Query mapping.
help.operation_timeout: Maximum wait for one business API request, from 1 to 30 seconds. It must also fit within the remaining run deadline. An uncertain POST outcome is checked separately rather than repeated.
help.customer_field: Input field containing the customer ID, usually customer_id. It must be required in the input schema and is checked against the client’s allowed customers. Required for POST; leave blank only for public read-only data.
help.public_voice: Make this GET operation available for public-data lookup during voice calls. Leave the customer identity field blank and grant the operation to the voice agent. Customer-specific voice lookup is not supported in this version.
help.remote_idempotency: Enable only if the business service supports the Idempotency-Key header. The request includes a stable operation key so the service can prevent duplicate records.
help.input_schema: JSON Schema defining the arguments the agent may send, their types and required fields. Example: {"type":"object","properties":{"customer_id":{"type":"string"}},"required":["customer_id"],"additionalProperties":false}.
help.output_schema: JSON Schema validating the result after Result projection. Example for an ID: {"type":"object","properties":{"id":{"type":"string"}},"required":["id"],"additionalProperties":false}. Only a valid result is returned to the agent.
help.query_mapping: JSON object mapping URL query parameter names to input field names. Example: {"customer":"customer_id"} sends ?customer=customer-1. Use {} when no query parameters are needed.
help.body_mapping: JSON object mapping fields in the POST body to input field names. Example: {"title":"summary","details":"description"}. Only these mapped input values are sent to the service.
help.result_projection: JSON object selecting service response fields returned to the agent. Keys are result field names; values are response paths. Example: {"id":"ticket.id"} extracts ticket.id as id. These fields must satisfy the result schema.
help.reconcile_operation: Optional GET operation ID in this connector used to check whether an uncertain POST created a record. Configure all three reconciliation fields together, or leave all blank. The check does not repeat the POST.
help.reconcile_argument: Input field of the checking GET operation that receives the original operation key, for example operation_id. The service must be able to find the record using this key.
help.reconcile_result_field: Field in the checking GET operation’s projected result whose nonempty value confirms the record exists, for example id. It must be defined in that operation’s result schema.
help.grant_agent: Choose which agent receives the selected published operations: Internal or External for voice calls, or Support request for API runs. Permissions are saved separately for each agent.
help.grant_operation: Allow the selected agent to call this exact connector operation and version. Publishing a new connector version does not grant it automatically. Voice agents can use only public read-only connector operations.
help.preset_name: Readable name for this text agent, for example Support requests. Applications invoke the fixed preset ID support-request and a published version.
help.model: OpenAI Responses model ID to use for API runs. Enter a model available to the selected OpenAI account that supports tool calls and structured results. This setting is separate from the voice model.
help.provider_credential: Select a saved OpenAI API key. Add it in the Connectors page’s Credentials section first. This authenticates text-model requests; business service credentials belong to their connectors.
help.instructions: Instructions describing how the text agent should handle customer lookups and support requests. The agent may use only the operations and customer IDs allowed by its published configuration and client permissions.
help.run_deadline: Maximum duration of the entire API run, including model responses and business API calls: 1–120 seconds. Work stops at the deadline; a business record already created is not undone.
help.output_budget: Total generated output-token budget shared across model responses in one run: 256–8192. A token is a piece of text. This limits output length, not total input tokens or total cost.
help.result_retention: Hours to keep the encrypted result after completion: 1–24. After expiry, applications cannot retrieve the result. Run status and history are retained separately.
help.preset_operation: Select the published connector operations this API agent may request. Also grant them to Support request on the Connectors page. An API client must be allowed to use the same operations.
help.published_version: Publishing creates a fixed version of the saved draft. API requests choose that version number. Later edits stay in the draft until published again; permissions must include the referenced connector versions.
help.client_id: Permanent name for the application receiving a token, for example crm. Use 1–48 lowercase letters, digits, hyphens or underscores, starting with a letter. Each client can access only its own runs and results.
help.authorized_customers: Customer IDs this client may use, separated by commas, for example customer-1, customer-2. Enter the IDs recognized by your business service. Up to 100 are allowed; wildcards are not supported.
help.client_expiry: How many days the new client token remains valid: 1–365. After expiry it cannot authenticate requests. You can revoke access earlier from the client list.
help.allow_create: Allow this client to submit a new API run. The requested customer, preset and operations must also be authorized.
help.allow_read: Allow this client to check the status and retrieve results of its own runs. It does not allow access to another client’s runs.
help.allow_cancel: Allow this client to request cancellation of its own runs. Cancellation stops further work but does not undo records already created in the business service.
help.allow_tickets: Permit explicitly requested ticket creation. The ticket operation must also be selected for the client, included in the published agent and granted on the Connectors page.
help.client_operation: Allow this client to use this exact published connector operation. It must also be included in the published API agent and granted to Support request.
help.request_client: Choose the client whose customer and operation permissions apply to this test. The administrator test uses those permissions and does not bypass them.
help.request_version: Published version number of the support-request agent to run. Save and publish the agent configuration first. A draft cannot be executed.
help.customer_id: Business-service customer ID for this request. It must match one of the selected client’s authorized customer IDs.
help.action: Customer lookup reads customer data. Create support ticket explicitly requests a new ticket. This test calls the configured OpenAI model and business service; it is not the offline emulator.
help.ticket_summary: Short title sent to the ticket service, up to 200 characters. Required when creating a ticket.
help.ticket_description: Details sent to the ticket service, up to 4000 characters. Required when creating a ticket; include the information the support team needs.
help.confirm_ticket: Confirm that this test may create a real ticket using the selected client’s permissions. Leave unchecked to prevent the test from submitting a write.
help.request_identity: Key identifying this logical request. Leave blank to generate one automatically. Reuse it only with the same request to retrieve the original run without creating another; change it for a new test.
help.workflow_ids: Published workflows with an API entrypoint that this client may execute. Add their agent IDs, separated by commas.
